ideas.name: PlatePilot
ideas.problem: The manual, high-stakes task of reconciling hundreds of individual guest dietary restrictions (allergies, intolerances, religious diets) against complex catering menus, which often leads to human error, expensive last-minute changes, or guest safety risks.
ideas.targetUser: Professional wedding planners and large-scale event coordinators managing high-end weddings (50-300+ guests) with multi-vendor catering requirements.
coreFeatures: Smart RSVP Data Ingestor (supports CSV, Excel, and WeddingWire/Zola exports)
AI-Powered Menu Contract Parser (extracts ingredients and options from PDF contracts)
Automated Mismatch Detection (flags high-risk conflicts like 'Nut Allergy' vs. 'Pesto Sauce')
One-Click Vendor Briefing Generator (exports categorized dietary summaries for catering teams)
realDependencies: AWS Textract or Google Cloud Vision for menu OCR
OpenAI GPT-4 API for natural language processing of unstructured dietary notes
Puppeteer or ReportLab for dynamic PDF generation
AWS S3 for secure document storage
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize 'Manifest-Based Mocking.' Instead of real OCR, the file upload component will detect specific filenames (e.g., 'Catering_Contract_A.pdf') and map them to hardcoded JSON 'Menu Objects.' The LLM reasoning will be simulated using a local keyword-matching engine that identifies specific conflicts (e.g., if 'nut' exists in guest data and 'walnut' exists in menu data, trigger a flag). To maintain realism, all 'processing' steps will include a randomized 1.5 to 3-second artificial delay with a loading spinner to simulate API latency. A pre-built 'Golden Dataset' of 50 guests and 3 caterer menus will be baked into the app to ensure a flawless, high-impact demonstration of mismatch detection.

ideas.name: GoalBridge
ideas.niche: Automated stimulus-to-clinical-goal documentation for Speech-Language Pathologists.
ideas.problem: The manual, time-consuming disconnect between hands-on therapeutic activities (using stimulus cards) and the administrative requirement to translate those specific interactions into formal, measurable, and insurance-compliant SOAP notes.
ideas.targetUser: Licensed Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs) working in high-volume school districts, private clinics, or medical settings who manage heavy caseloads and face significant administrative burnout.
coreFeatures: Digital Stimulus Library: A searchable repository of visual/auditory stimulus cards (phonemes, articulation, vocabulary) that can be activated during a session.
One-Tap Goal Mapping: A drag-and-drop interface that allows therapists to instantly link a stimulus card to a specific IEP or clinical progress goal.
Auto-SOAP Synthesizer: An intelligent engine that converts stimulus usage data and session performance into structured 'Assessment' and 'Plan' text for clinical documentation.
Mastery Analytics Dashboard: A visual reporting tool that correlates specific stimulus types with goal attainment trends to provide evidence for clinical progress.
realDependencies: HIPAA-compliant cloud infrastructure (AWS or Azure)
Encrypted relational database for patient-specific goal tracking
Secure Authentication provider (Auth0 or Okta) for practitioner identity
PDF generation engine for exporting formal clinical reports
ideas.emulationStrategy: The prototype will use a local JSON-based 'MockDataStore' containing pre-populated patients, goals, and stimulus cards to avoid actual database calls. All asynchronous operations (e.g., 'Saving Note' or 'Syncing Library') will be wrapped in a custom 'simulateNetworkCall' function that uses a randomized delay between 600ms and 1800ms to trigger and display realistic loading spinners. Instead of actual PDF generation, the app will trigger a high-fidelity CSS-styled 'Report Preview' modal that mimics the look of a formal document. Authentication will be bypassed via a single 'Enter Demo Mode' button that bypasses the login flow and injects a hardcoded 'Demo Therapist' profile into the app state.

ideas.name: Nodal
ideas.niche: Curriculum-centric mastery tracking and concept-gap analysis for professional educators.
ideas.problem: Tutors lack a granular way to visualize and communicate specific knowledge gaps, making it difficult to prove ROI to parents and plan evidence-based lesson paths.
ideas.targetUser: Independent high-end academic tutors and boutique tutoring firm owners specializing in STEM and standardized test prep who manage 5+ students and require professional reporting tools.
coreFeatures: Hierarchical Curriculum Node Builder: Create nested learning taxonomies to map specific sub-concepts (e.g., Calculus -> Derivatives -> Power Rule).
Mastery Heatmap Dashboard: A visual color-coded grid representing real-time student proficiency across the entire curriculum tree.
Smart Gap-Priority Planner: An automated lesson suggestion engine that ranks upcoming topics based on the highest 'learning debt' or failed node checks.
Automated Parent Progress Reports: Polished, one-click visual summaries that translate mastery data into readable, professional progress narratives.
realDependencies: PostgreSQL with recursive CTE support for managing deep hierarchical curriculum trees
OpenAI GPT-4 API for generating pedagogical lesson suggestions from mastery data
Auth0 for multi-role authentication (Tutor vs. Parent)
Stripe API for subscription billing and per-student seat management
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'mock_db.json' containing a pre-built Algebra II curriculum tree and three sample student profiles with varying mastery levels. The AI Lesson Planner will be emulated via a function that simulates a 2.5-second processing delay using a Promise, then returns a template-based suggestion using the 'current_node' key. Authentication will be a bypassable hardcoded toggle. All 'API calls' will be wrapped in a helper function that injects random latency between 200ms and 1200ms to simulate real-world network variability.

ideas.name: LuminaSight
ideas.niche: Art Gallery Curator Lighting & Sightline Planner
ideas.problem: The inability to accurately pre-visualize how specific light intensities, angles, and visitor perspectives will interact with sensitive artworks, leading to potential light damage or suboptimal exhibition layouts.
ideas.targetUser: Museum curators, exhibition designers, and lighting specialists managing high-value collections in professional galleries and cultural institutions.
coreFeatures: 3D Spatial Scene Builder for importing or modeling gallery layouts
Dynamic Lux & Kelvin Simulation to model light intensity and color temperature
Virtual Sightline Mapping to project visitor perspectives from varying heights
Sensitivity Threshold Alerts to prevent over-exposure of delicate pigments
realDependencies: Three.js or Babylon.js for high-fidelity 3D web rendering
CAD/BIM file parser API (e.g., Autodesk Forge) for architectural imports
Manufacturer Lighting Specification API for real-world fixture data
High-performance Ray Tracing engine for accurate light bounce simulation
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a static Three.js environment with predefined JSON-based room coordinates. The CAD import will be simulated with a 3-second progress bar that triggers a transition to a hardcoded room model. Lighting calculations will be faked using a simple proximity-based mathematical formula (1/d^2) rather than actual ray-tracing to simulate lux drops. API calls for light fixture specs will be intercepted and resolved from a local mock JSON object with a randomized 500ms-1500ms delay to mimic real network latency.

ideas.name: K9Flow
ideas.niche: Behavioral sequence mapping and trigger-pattern analysis for professional canine behaviorists.
ideas.problem: The inability to accurately visualize the chronological chain of events (trigger -> physiological response -> behavior) prevents trainers from identifying subtle patterns and providing professional, data-backed reports to clients.
ideas.targetUser: Certified professional dog trainers and veterinary behaviorists managing high-stakes reactivity or aggression cases who require precision logging and client-facing documentation.
coreFeatures: Timeline Sequence Builder: A drag-and-drop interface to map the exact order of triggers, physiological cues, and outward behaviors.
Trigger Intensity Heatmaps: Visual analytics that correlate environmental factors (noise, density, motion) with behavioral outbursts.
Client Progress PDF Engine: One-tap generation of structured, professional reports summarizing behavioral trends over time.
Contextual Tagging System: Quick-log tools for time of day, weather, location, and human handler presence.
realDependencies: Google Maps API for geolocation/environmental tagging
Firebase Realtime Database for multi-device sync
AWS S3 for video/photo behavior evidence storage
Puppeteer or PDFKit for automated report generation
ideas.emulationStrategy: Implement a local Mock Service Worker (MSW) to intercept all fetch requests. Use a pre-defined 'behavior_scenarios.json' file to return complex, realistic datasets with intentional 500ms to 1500ms artificial delays to simulate network latency. For geolocation, the app will return hardcoded 'Training Park' coordinates rather than actual GPS data. For the PDF Engine, the app will trigger a fake 3-second loading progress bar and then return a static link to a local sample PDF file to simulate successful cloud generation.
